reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that in-match hydration breaks act as natural experiments where each match serves as its own control. The case-crossover design leverages this by comparing moments immediately before and after the break, thereby eliminating match-specific confounders such as team quality, stadium, and era. The key mathematical innovation lies in the use of fixed-effects ANCOVA with clustered standard errors to estimate the Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATT) at break times. This approach allows for robust inference even in high-dimensional settings where traditional regression fails due to omitted variable bias. The sign-adjusted momentum index ensures directional consistency in measuring momentum shifts, while the quadratic time trend captures non-linear temporal dynamics. The model assumes that the break’s impact is localized and that the pre-break momentum state is predictive of post-break behavior. Failure modes include misalignment of control windows, insufficient data for estimation, or violation of independence assumptions due to overlapping stoppages.
